thread:
neil: Quick sync we ran the extended microbench on Harbor-14b (int6) and I want to propose a lightweight canary/scorecard before any GTN push.

maya: Good call. Can you share the topline?

neil: Topline from 2k queries across product slices (search, summarization, chat, rerank):
```
Harbor-14b-int6 - microbench (2k total, weighted slice mix)
latency P50: 165ms, P95: 390ms
avg_tokens_per_resp: 38
cost_per_token_est: $0.0115
weighted_cost_per_req: $0.437
baseline (current-13b-int8) weighted_cost_per_req: $0.79
net_delta: ~44.6% cost reduction
quality delta (macro): search recall -0.5%, summarize ROUGE-L +0.4, chat human_pass 83% vs 86% baseline
```

maya: Chat human pass still a pinch low. Any patterns on failure modes?

sumi: Yes chat failures concentrated on: long-system prompts truncating, multi-step reasoning (math chains), and list formatting. Single-turn clarity is fine.

neil: We also saw slight rerank ranking shifts for specific edge queries (very similar titles). Not large but noticeable in automated fluency score.

chris: From product side: we can tolerate minor rerank deviations if user-facing recall/search is within noise. Chat reductions are more visible. Suggest partial routing.

maya: Proposed Lighthouse canary gates (recommend):
- pass_size: 2k A/B across slices
- thresholds: chat_human_pass >= 85%, search_recall_delta >= -1.0%, P95 <= 450ms, net_cost_savings >= 30%
- guardrails: if chat fails, route chat intent to baseline, allow Harbor for search/summarize/rerank

sumi: +1. Also add a quant-sensitivity sub-sweep: int6 vs int8 on the 3 failure categories. 1k queries each.

neil: Ops ask: can we implement intent-based split and capacity-aware fallback? I.e., prefer Harbor for non-chat but if GPU pool is saturated fall back to prod model instead of queueing.

ops-bot: routing-toggle created: `harbor_canary_v2`. Feature flag: `harbor.canary.v2=on` toggles 20% traffic for non-chat intents by intent-tagger. Fallback policy: capacity->model-fallback immediate. Rollback ready.

chris: For GTN guidance blurb, propose two bullets: 1) expected 35-45% cost savings on eligible requests; 2) conservative rollout: enable search/summarize first, hold chat until sweep confirms priming stability.

maya: I'll run the quant-sensitivity sweep tomorrow AM and push results here. If int8 reduces chat regression by >2pp with small cost increase, we can consider hybrid routing (int8 for chat, int6 for others).

sumi: Quick microbench ask: include token-level breakdown and per-route latency bucket (small/medium/long responses). That helped legal/product last time.

neil: Agreed. Also record median tokens and tail tokens separately so GTN gets an expected cost per session.

ops-bot: canary job scheduled: `harbor_int6_quant_sweep_2026-03-24`. Job ID 78921. Results will be posted to this thread when complete.

chris: Thanks after results, we should draft a 150-200 word GTN note + 2 slide summary for ops/product. I'll take the text if someone drops numbers.

maya: Will post sweep results and an updated lighthouse scorecard (CSV snippet + pass/fail) here. Plan: keep default off until we hit gates.

neil: Solid. Tag me when ops-bot posts results.

chris: One open Q: how does this interact with dedicated pools for enterprise customers? If dedicated customers prefer baseline for consistency we should exclude them from the canary by default.

maya: Good point. We'll scope canary to hosted tenants only and add explicit opt-in for dedicated customers.

sumi: OK sounds like a plan. Thanks everyone.
